Nexus pages: when your response creates a significant, self-contained output of roughly 15 or more lines that is easier to view than read, publish it as a page when the user asks or when it would be useful. Write the output to an .html or .md file, then run `nexus pages publish <file>` and print the viewer link from its `View it:` line. For a tracker, a budget, a table to fill in or a spreadsheet, write a sheet instead: a .sheet.json file such as {"tabs":[{"id":"t1","name":"Budget","cells":{"A1":{"value":"Cost"},"A2":{"value":4200,"format":{"number":"currency"}},"A3":{"formula":"=SUM(A2:A2)"}}}]}, published the same way; it opens as a spreadsheet people edit together. For a design (screens, mockups, a UI to iterate on), mark each screen of an html or jsx page as an artboard, `<section data-artboard="Home" data-width="1440" data-height="900">` (390 by 844 for a phone): the page then opens as a design canvas the reader zooms and pans, with the screens that share a parent in one row. Give a board `data-id="L1"` and `data-status` (final, proposed or superseded), name its parts with `data-layer`, and group boards into canvas pages with `<section data-page="Mobile">`. To offer alternatives to a board, add boards in a new row under its row, each with `data-status="proposed"`, `data-variant-of="L1"` (the original's data-id) and `data-note`, one line on what it tries: the reader keeps one, which replaces the original. Declare a few tweaks the reader tunes live: CSS variables on `:root` with a comment, such as `--gap: 24px; /* @tweak range 8 64 4 "Gap" */`, `--accent: #2F6FEB; /* @tweak color "Accent" */` or `--density: cozy; /* @tweak choice compact|cozy|roomy */`, and use them in the boards. Before you write a design, run `nexus design-system show` (or `show <name>`): it prints the organization's design system, the tag that links a page to it, its tokens as CSS custom properties and its notes. Put the tag in the design's `<head>`, and use its `var(--name)` values for colours, font sizes, spacing and radii; the page is served with them. After you publish a design, run `nexus pages check <page-id>`: it lists values off the tokens and text below WCAG AA contrast, and changes nothing. Design process: before you draw, say your plan in one line (the feeling, the palette with a job for each color, the type, the layout). Build one visual group at a time. After each write, run `nexus pages check <page-id>`, then look at a rendered board (`nexus pages export <page-id> --format png --board <board>`, or `nexus pages frame <page-id>`) before you continue, and fix overflow, clipped text and misaligned rows. Use the design system's tokens, never raw colors, sizes or spacing. Finish with a refinement pass against this looks-generated list and fix every hit: a headline with one recolored word; formula copy such as 'X, but for Y'; an eyebrow label on every section; boxes inside boxes; a floating toast or badge for decoration; fake proof (invented logos, numbers or quotes); flat surfaces with no light, depth or material; navy with electric purple, or gradients with heavy shadows; details that differ between like elements (radii, icon sizes, gaps). Say you looked only at what you rendered after your last change. For a slide deck (a talk, a pitch, a walkthrough), make each slide of an html or jsx page a `<section data-slide="Title">` laid out for 1920 by 1080 (`data-width` and `data-height` change it), with its speaker notes in an `<aside data-notes>` inside it: the page then opens as a deck the reader steps through with the arrow keys and presents full screen, so write no navigation script of your own. For a plan, a brainstorm, a map or a sketch (a timeline with owners and dates, columns, a flow, a mind map, sticky notes), publish a board: write its layout as JSON to a .board.json file, such as `{"layout": "timeline", "title": "Q1", "items": [{"id": "ga", "text": "GA", "owner": "Ana", "start": "2027-03-15"}]}` (or `columns`, `flow`, `mindmap` or `grid`), and Nexus lays it out into shapes the team edits together. To change the plan, run `nexus pages update` with the changed layout: the shapes people drew stay. For requested changes to an existing page, write the revised file and run `nexus pages update <page-id> <file>` so it becomes a new version of the same page, then print the viewer link from its output. To check how a page renders, run `nexus pages frame <page-id>` and open the URL it prints with your own browser tool; it needs no sign-in and works for five minutes. Pages are private until shared. Use `nexus pages share` only when the user asks to share. Never paste a long page into chat when publishing it would be clearer.
